title: Global Oil Refining Outlook | BloombergNEF
gist: BloombergNEF expects about 4.2m b/d of net global refining capacity growth in 2026-2030, ~95% in Africa and Asia Pacific, well above refined product demand growth, creating overhang risk for utilization and margins, especially for less-competitive assets. The Iran war has tightened product markets and favored Atlantic Basin refiners without yet changing the medium-term pipeline.

insights.claim: BloombergNEF expects roughly 4.2 million b/d of net global oil refining capacity growth from 2026 through 2030, up 162% from the preceding five years, based on asset-level tracking.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: A sharp reversal from subdued additions signals a supply wave in refined products later this decade.

insights.claim: Refining capacity growth projected for 2026-2030 is well above projected growth in refined product demand and would reverse several years of subdued additions and elevated closures.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Supply outpacing demand growth is the basis for a structural margin headwind for refiners.
insights.locator: Global oil refining capacity growth could rebound

insights.claim: Half of the 2026-2030 capacity additions are already operational or under construction, per BNEF tracking.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Half of the wave is relatively locked in, while the rest is uncertain and could slip.

insights.claim: If all projects materialize, a refining capacity overhang could intensify competition and weigh on utilization and margins, particularly for less-competitive assets.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Favor competitive, integrated refiners; watch marginal assets for closures and weak margins.
insights.quote: a capacity overhang could intensify competition and weigh on utilization and margins, particularly for less-competitive assets
insights.locator: Global oil refining capacity growth could rebound

insights.claim: Confidence in capacity additions declines later in the decade because a larger share of 2028-2030 capacity is at earlier stages, leaving it at greater risk of delay and cancellation.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Projected overhang may be overstated; delays and cancellations would ease margin pressure.

insights.claim: Africa and Asia Pacific account for roughly 95% of global net refining capacity growth through 2030, driven by stronger demand outlooks, import-substitution strategies and export-oriented, petrochemical-integrated assets.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Growth in refining and petrochemical integration is concentrated in emerging markets, shifting trade balances.
insights.locator: Africa and Asia Pacific account for roughly 95%

insights.claim: China and India account for 71% of total refining capacity additions in 2026 and 2027, and most of those are operational or under construction.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Near-term supply additions are highly visible and concentrated in two countries.

insights.claim: China faces a refining supply overhang that may lead to further consolidation among smaller independent refiners, while India and Africa add capacity for greater self-sufficiency.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Expect Chinese independent refiner consolidation and reduced import dependence in India and Africa.
insights.locator: Crude oil and product trade flows will change unevenly

insights.claim: Europe and the US may experience further refinery closures as new capacity is built elsewhere.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Western refiners face structural pressure from lower-cost, newer capacity in Asia and Africa.
insights.locator: Crude oil and product trade flows will change unevenly

insights.claim: The Iran war has disrupted flows of Middle East refining and Persian Gulf feedstocks, tightening product markets and shifting the advantage toward Atlantic Basin refiners.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: Atlantic Basin refiners benefit near term from tight product markets.
insights.locator: The Iran war has disrupted flows

insights.claim: BNEF sees limited impact of the Iran conflict on the medium-term refining capacity pipeline so far, while it strengthens the case for resilience investment in storage, pipelines and logistics.
insights.speaker: BloombergNEF
insights.so_what: The war is a near-term trade; the supply wave thesis is intact, and logistics infrastructure gains a tailwind.
insights.locator: The Iran war has disrupted flows
